content.user_title: Build and Review Cloudflare Gateway Workers
content.value_statement: Gateway Forward integrations require entrypoints, context handling, and continuation rules that differ from ordinary Workers. This skill guides implementation and validation using current Cloudflare references.
actual_capabilities: Guide implementation of the named GatewayMiddleware RPC entrypoint and its handle method.
Explain zero-or-one request continuation and the differences between next() and independent fetch() subrequests.
Guide trusted identity and device posture access, including optional values and lookup failures.
Review Gateway inspection order, supported traffic, decryption requirements, and invocation failure behavior.
Recommend type checks, scoped Gateway integration tests, valid response statuses, and streaming behavior.
limitations: Provides instructions and reference links, not bundled implementation scripts or executable tests.
Requires current Cloudflare documentation and installed Gateway types for exact API details.
Gateway path validation requires an existing Worker and a configured, scoped Forward policy.
WebSockets bypass the Worker, and matching Workers VPC traffic is dropped.

use_cases.description: Adapt an existing Worker to the named RPC entrypoint and correct continuation contract.

use_cases.title: Review identity-dependent behavior
use_cases.description: Check identity trust, posture lookups, missing values, and lookup failures before introducing identity-dependent decisions.

use_cases.title: Validate a scoped rollout

prompt_templates.title: Understand the entrypoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how GatewayMiddleware differs from a default fetch handler, using the current Forward guide.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the Gateway Forward contract.

prompt_templates.title: Review continuation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Worker for zero-or-one next() calls, synthetic responses, and independent fetch() subrequests. Explain any policy inheritance implications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review request flow before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Check identity handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Gateway identity and posture handling. Distinguish anonymous users, absent posture values, and rejected lookups. Recommend explicit failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan integration validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scoped Gateway test plan for this Worker. Cover RPC entrypoints, continuation, inspection order, streaming, response restrictions, and traffic limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a controlled integration rollout.

output_examples.input: Review a Worker that only implements a default fetch handler.
output: The default handler does not implement the Gateway Forward contract.
Export GatewayMiddleware extending WorkerEntrypoint and implement its handle method.
Validate the named RPC entrypoint and a permitted request through a scoped Forward policy.

output_examples.input: Review a Worker that changes the destination and calls next() twice.
output: Call next() at most once; it always targets the original destination.
Destination URL and host changes do not redirect continuation.
A separate fetch() subrequest does not inherit the user Gateway policies or egress configuration.

output_examples.input: Review a Worker that trusts identity headers and buffers all response bodies.
output: Use Gateway-provided identity instead of client-supplied identity headers.
Handle rejected identity lookups separately from anonymous identity values.
Stream response bodies and omit bodies for HEAD requests and statuses 204, 205, and 304.

best_practices: Consult current Forward documentation and type-check against installed Gateway types before implementation.
Use Gateway identity and explicitly handle missing context values and rejected lookups.
Test the named RPC entrypoint and a scoped Gateway path, including continuation and streaming behavior.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful direct fetch-handler request as proof that Gateway integration works.
Using next() to redirect, retry, fan out, or continue more than once.
Assuming independent fetch() subrequests inherit Gateway policies or egress configuration.

faq.question: Does a default fetch handler implement Gateway Forward?
faq.answer: No. Gateway invokes the named GatewayMiddleware handle method through RPC.

faq.question: Can next() redirect a request to another destination?
faq.answer: No. It targets the original destination and ignores destination URL or host changes.

faq.question: Do independent fetch() subrequests inherit Gateway policies?
faq.answer: No. They do not inherit the user Gateway policies or egress configuration.

faq.question: How should identity lookup failures be handled?
faq.answer: Catch lookup failures separately from anonymous identity values and define explicit behavior when the Worker depends on identity.

faq.question: Which traffic limitations should I check?
faq.answer: HTTPS requires decryption, WebSockets bypass the Worker, and matching Workers VPC traffic is dropped. Consult current documentation for additional limitations.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy or test a Worker automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation and validation guidance and references related skills for project setup and deployment.
